correctness.rationale: All r≥1, all fixed real c, the exact exponent restriction, limit variable and sharp extremal sequence are explicit. Factorwise monotonicity + Mertens/PNT yield λ_r on the restricted family, Poisson CLT supplies Φ(c). At criticality, first-order Poisson lattice Edgeworth expansion and quantitative Mertens yield a uniform O(1/x) residual; vanishing phase mesh proves infinitely many signs for r≤4, whereas Mills/zeta comparisons give c_r>2 and eventual reversal on extremal powers for r≥5. Standard-library verifier passed 18 independent finite Poisson correction checks, Euler products, quantile sign and mesh. Finite checks do not certify infinitude.

value.rationale: The source poses reducing the truncated-exponential order as a natural challenge. The answer identifies the exact central-limit width and its sharp zeta-normal threshold across all bounded prime exponents; the subtle lattice correction shows a genuine phase change between r=4 and r=5 even at criticality. This is a structural, quantitatively optimal theorem, not merely finite casework, parameter renaming or a textbook one-line corollary.
